Subject: Packaging & region eligibility for multi-cloud listing — SeaStart pilot

Hi all,

We need to lock the per-cloud packaging and regional eligibility for the SeaStart pilot so Marissa can finish the marketplace submission forms this week. Attached is a first-pass "proposed-pack-matrix.xlsx" with three candidate bundles (Core, Scale, Enterprise) and suggested regional coverage per cloud.

Top asks:
- Confirm which bundle(s) we want listed on each marketplace (AWS SaaS, Azure Marketplace SaaS Offers, GCP Marketplace).
- Flag any cloud-specific exclusions (GovCloud, Azure Government, GCP restricted regions).
- Recommend the canonical SKU names and 1-line descriptions we should put in the listings (Marissa will use these verbatim).
- Approve co-sell readiness items (pricing parity, required legal text, allowed demonstration environments).

Notes: SeaStart is prioritizing Azure for a pilot with a federal-contracted customer in mid-August, but they want AWS/GCP listings available for non-federal proofs. I put a conservative default in the matrix: Enterprise = global (non-Gov), Scale = us-west/us-east + eu-west, Core = US-only for initial launch.

Please reply with firm yes/no or edits by EOD PST so Marissa can submit the forms on Wednesday.

Thanks,
Laura

Subject: Re: Packaging & region eligibility for multi-cloud listing — SeaStart pilot

Laura — thanks for the matrix, looks useful. A few immediate constraints from the AWS side and marketplace ops perspective:

- AWS Marketplace (SaaS) requires a distinct SKU per pricing model. If we expose Core/Scale/Enterprise as separate SKUs, we should expect separate metering & pricing configs. For quick go-to-market, consider launching with Core + Enterprise only; Scale can be a private/quote-only SKU behind a listing.
- GovCloud: AWS requires an explicit GovCloud listing and a separate seller registration (and in many cases a different AMI/packaging). If SeaStart's federal customer needs procurement via AWS GovCloud, we need to fast-track GovCloud enrollment — it's a 2–3 week process and may require an alternate account.
- AWS co-sell: to enable partner-led co-sell, pricing parity across channels is necessary and we must have the commercial terms in the listing docs. We should pre-fill the "co-sell readiness" checklist with expected discounts and reference implementation links.

Suggested immediate decisions:
1) AWS: List Core (public), Enterprise (public) — mark Scale as "private/quote" for now.
2) Azure: prioritize for pilot (see Marissa's form) but implement Enterprise gating for Gov deployments.
3) GCP: GCP Marketplace has fewer enforced SKU types; we can mirror AWS's public/quote split.

I'll loop in marketplace ops to confirm if the Core public SKU can be on both AWS and GCP without separate billing integration.

-ben

--
Ben Carter
Head of Cloud GTM | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Laura / team — quick technical constraints and a recommendation from Product: 

- Packaging: Our runtime supports identical inference binaries across clouds, but we ship tuned quantized variants. The marketplace listing should call out the model class and a "recommended instance family" per SKU (e.g., Scale = g5/GPU-backed; Core = cpu-backed). Avoid promising specific GPU types in the public description; use guidance in the technical detail page.
- Regional quotas: for Enterprise tier, we should pre-allocate regional capacity in us-east-1, us-west-2, and europe-west1 for the launch. For Azure, include West US 2 and North Europe.
- Security-sensitive regions: Azure Government and AWS GovCloud require separate offer metadata and different endpoint URLs; don't list Enterprise in GovCloud until we complete the SCCM (security control matrix) and KMS/HSM integration. That will probably push Gov availability to September.
- SKU naming: proposed canonical SKUs: RDW-SeaStart-Core, RDW-SeaStart-Scale, RDW-SeaStart-Enterprise. Avoid spaces and special characters — marketplace forms often reject them.

Recommendation: Approve the matrix with the following edits:
- Core: public on AWS + GCP (US only), minimal instance guidance, low quota.
- Scale: private/quote on all clouds for now; listed as "contact sales".
- Enterprise: public on Azure + AWS (non-Gov) with explicit capacity zones; Gov support = "coming soon".

I can add the technical copy for the listing pages (instance guidance, expected latency, throughput) if Marissa sends the exact fields required by each marketplace.

-Karthik

Thanks, Laura and team — this looks comprehensive. A few items from SeaStart's side:

- Our federal customer requires Azure as the procurement route (they purchase through Azure Marketplace). They are OK with "Enterprise" only for the pilot but would like Enterprise to include an initial 6-month SOW-based commitment (we're fine with that being quote-only in AWS/GCP).
- Timeline is tight: procurement kicks off July 28 and they want an Azure offer visible to their procurement portal by Aug 5.
- We can accept the SKU names Karthik proposed. If Azure requires a separate Gov SKU, SeaStart will sign the enrollment forms and provide the necessary attestation, but we need Redwood to own the GovCloud seller registration steps.

If you can prioritize Azure Enterprise + Gov enrollment tasks, we will hold off on pushing Scale live.

Best,
Anna

Thanks for the quick inputs — summary and actions below. I'll treat this thread as the formal decision log for Marissa to proceed with marketplace submissions.

Decisions (approved):
- SKU names: RDW-SeaStart-Core, RDW-SeaStart-Scale (quote), RDW-SeaStart-Enterprise (approved).
- AWS: Core = public (US only), Enterprise = public (non-Gov), Scale = private/quote. Ben to confirm billing integration details with marketplace ops.
- Azure: Prioritize Enterprise for the pilot; start Gov enrollment now. Marissa, please use the Enterprise copy Karthik will provide and mark Gov availability as "coming soon" until SCCM/KMS items are complete.
- GCP: Mirror AWS public/quote split for now.

Action items:
- Marissa Cole: submit Azure Enterprise offer by July 23 with Enterprise copy; attach SeaStart SOW placeholder and our co-sell checklist. (owner: marissa.cole@redwood.ai)
- Ben Carter: confirm with marketplace ops whether Core can share billing integration across AWS and GCP (owner: ben.carter@redwood.ai).
- Karthik Iyer: provide technical listing copy (instance guidance, latency examples, required minimums) by EOD July 21.
- Laura Bennett: own GovCloud seller enrollment process; will coordinate with SeaStart for attestations.

I'll update the shared doc and HubSpot record once Marissa has submitted the forms. Thanks everyone — good momentum.

Laura
